items.title: Report out-of-date installed bundled skills
items.body:
## Problem

`glab skills install` copies a bundled skill into a skills directory, for example `~/.agents/skills/`. After a glab upgrade, the binary ships a newer bundled skill, but the installed copy stays at its old version until someone runs `glab skills update`.

An agent reading the stale copy can follow instructions for commands or flags that have since changed, which is the gap the `Bundled skills` review rule and `TestBundledSkillsUseRealCommandsAndFlags` close for the bundled copy (https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4336).

Raised in review: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4336#note_4178734429

## Proposal

Have glab report when an installed bundled skill is older than the one in the binary, and point to `glab skills update`.

Open questions:

- Where to report it: on any command (like the update notifier), only on `glab skills` commands, or both.
- How to detect staleness: compare content, or record the glab version that installed the skill.
- Whether Duo Developer environments install skills fresh each session, or can carry an old copy across upgrades. That decides how urgent this is.

items.title: Add a Duo Code Review rule to keep bundled skills in sync with command changes
items.body:
## Problem

The bundled agent skills in `internal/commands/skills/bundled/assets/` (`glab` and `glab-stack`) describe how agents should run `glab` commands. When an MR changes a command's user-visible contract, nothing prompts the author to update the matching `SKILL.md`, so agents can follow instructions that fail, hang, or leave work unfinished.

Example: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4267 made `glab stack reorder` and `glab stack infer` usable without a TTY. Its skill update left out that `infer` needs `--name` when no stack is active, that `reorder` must be followed by `glab stack sync`, and how to recover from reorder conflicts. Those gaps were fixed afterwards in https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/4335.

## Proposal

Add a `Bundled skills` block to `.gitlab/duo/mr-review-instructions.yaml`, scoped to non-test command code. It maps command paths to skills and asks Duo to:

- flag contract changes (`Use` or arguments, added, renamed, or removed flags, TTY, prompt, or editor requirements, new required follow-up steps) that leave the matching `SKILL.md` stale
- when the MR updates a skill, check that its commands work as written for an agent without a TTY
- ignore internal refactors, test-only changes, and help-text wording changes

## Possible follow-up

A deterministic check that flags any `glab <cmd> --flag` in a `SKILL.md` that no longer exists in the cobra command tree. It would catch removals and renames only, but it can't miss them.

items.title: Add RPM (dnf) support to glab artifact-registry
items.body:
### Problem to solve

As a platform engineer, I want `glab` to set up `dnf` for a GitLab Artifact Registry RPM repository and keep it working, so a long-lived host or a CI runner does not need its own token refresh job.

Artifact Registry's hosted RPM repositories (spec S38, https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/ops/artifact-registry/-/merge_requests/3497) serve `dnf` with HTTP Basic. The password is a token from the token exchange, and it expires after at most 12 hours.

- `dnf` has no credential helper. It reads the token from the `.repo` file, so a host that stays current needs a job that rewrites the file.
- At a signing key rotation, `dnf` asks to confirm the new key. A host with no terminal fails until someone imports it.
- `dnf5` (Fedora) never sends credentials to `gpgkey=`. On a private repository, the user downloads the key by hand, and again at each rotation.

### Proposal

Add `glab artifact-registry login --dnf --registry <repository URL>`:

1. Write the `.repo` file under `/etc/yum.repos.d/` with `baseurl`, `username`, `password`, `repo_gpgcheck=1`, `gpgcheck=0` and `gpgkey`, readable only by root.
1. Refresh the token on a timer, before it expires.
1. Import the repository's public keys after checking each fingerprint against the Artifact Registry API, so a key rotation needs no prompt. For `dnf5`, write the keys to a local file and point `gpgkey=file://` at it.

### Further details

- The timer still needs a credential that lasts longer than 12 hours. So this moves the long-lived credential into `glab`; it does not remove it.
- During a rotation, `repomd.xml.key` serves the current key and the other key.
- The API routes that return a key's fingerprint are not decided yet. ADR-030 owns them.

### Links / references

- RPM format work item: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/605699
- Artifact Registry RPM hosted spec: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/ops/artifact-registry/-/merge_requests/3497
- ADR-030, repository signing keys: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/ops/artifact-registry/-/merge_requests/3768
- Go support in the same command: https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8667
